claims.text: Mechanical-property differences among equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its subsets are governed by the interaction of lattice distortion and electronic structure.
Lattice distortion and electronic structure influence dislocation mobility.
Changes in dislocation mobility govern alloy strength and ductility.
Systematically varying constituent elements alters lattice distortion.
Systematically varying constituent elements alters electronic structure.
Alloys with greater lattice distortion will have higher strength than the equiatomic quinary baseline.
Alloys with greater lattice distortion will have lower ductility than the equiatomic quinary baseline.
Specific electronic-structure features will be associated with higher strength than the equiatomic quinary baseline.
Specific electronic-structure features will be associated with lower ductility than the equiatomic quinary baseline.
The proposed relationship applies to single-phase FCC alloys containing three to five constituents.
The investigation is to be performed at room temperature under uniaxial tensile loading.
A lack of correlation between lattice distortion, electronic structure, and mechanical properties across the alloy series would falsify the hypothesis.
